name: Large multi-site community hospital corporation (Ontario)
modelled_on: Halton Healthcare (Oakville Trafalgar Memorial, Milton District and Georgetown hospitals), from its 2018/19, 2020/21 and 2021/22 annual community reports and public service listing; Ontario Health and CIHI public material for provincial rules and reporting.
summary: A not-for-profit public hospital corporation that runs three community hospitals in a fast-growing suburban region of Ontario, with about 640 inpatient beds and an emergency department at each site. It treats about 160,000 emergency visits, 4,000 to 4,700 births and 40,000 to 45,000 surgeries a year, and runs inpatient medicine, intensive care, mental health, dialysis, chemotherapy, outpatient clinics, diagnostic imaging and a hospital laboratory. Patients do not pay for insured care: about four-fifths of its roughly $475 million to $590 million annual revenue comes from the Ontario Ministry of Health through a global budget and per-procedure funding, managed under an accountability agreement with the regional health authority (Ontario Health from 2021), with the rest from preferred accommodation, parking, retail, uninsured patients and other grants. Physicians, midwives and dentists hold privileges and bill the province directly; about 4,900 employees, most of them unionized nurses and support staff, work in clinical programs (emergency, medicine, surgery, women's and children's, mental health, diagnostics, ambulatory care and clinical support) and corporate departments (finance, people, digital health, facilities, quality). A volunteer board governs it, advised on medical matters by a Medical Advisory Committee, and it is accredited by Accreditation Canada. From 2020 to 2022 it also ran COVID-19 testing, vaccination and field hospitals.

process_map.name: Receive ambulance patients and transfer care
process_map.description: Paramedics bring a patient to the ambulance bay, a triage nurse takes verbal handover and triages, and the patient stays on the paramedic stretcher until an ED space and nurse are free. Offload delay ties up ambulances and is tracked by the region.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the usual December-March rise in ED visits and admissions in Ontario community hospitals.

Volume from hosp-ed-ambulance-offload (2026-11-24): 20% of Ontario ED visits arrived by ambulance in 2022/23 (OAG 2023) applied to the corporation's 126,357-161,049 ED visits a year (annual reports), divided by 12. The organisation file's 2,800 a month implies about 21-26% by ambulance.

process_map.name: Triage and register emergency patients
process_map.description: A triage nurse takes the chief complaint and vital signs and assigns a Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale level from 1 to 5, and a registration clerk validates the health card and opens the visit. Queues build at shift change and in the evening, and acuity drift is a known error.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the usual December-March rise in ED visits and admissions in Ontario community hospitals.
Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Assess, investigate and treat emergency patients
process_map.description: An emergency physician sees the patient in order of acuity and wait, orders tests, imaging and medications, reassesses when results return and decides whether to discharge, consult, admit or transfer. Waiting for results and consultants makes up most of the visit.
process_map.unit_of_work: one ED visit seen by a physician

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the usual December-March rise in ED visits and admissions in Ontario community hospitals.
Provincial ED length-of-stay targets (src7) shape the process; volume is ED visits less about 3% who leave without being seen (author's estimate).

process_map.name: Obtain specialist consultations in the emergency department
process_map.description: The emergency physician pages the on-call specialist, such as internal medicine, general surgery or orthopaedics, who comes in or advises by phone. Consultants often finish their own lists first, so the patient waits on a stretcher for hours.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 15% of ED visits get a specialist consultation.

process_map.name: Admit emergency patients and hold them until a bed is free
process_map.description: After the decision to admit, the ED requests a bed, gives admission orders and keeps caring for the patient on an ED stretcher until patient flow assigns a bed and the unit accepts report. Boarded patients occupy ED spaces and are the main cause of long ED stays.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: occupancy runs above 100% in winter with unfunded surge beds in hallways and lounges.

Volume from hosp-ed-admission-boarding (2026-11-24): ED visits of 10,530 to 13,420 a month (organisation file) times the admitted share of NACRS visits: 10.6% in 2018/19 and 2019/20, 12.4% in 2020/21 and 11.2% in 2021/22 (cihi_nacrs); OAG reports 12% in 2022/23. The organisation file's 1,100 to 1,600 (mode 1,350) implies about 10.4% and is close.

process_map.name: Discharge emergency patients home with follow-up
process_map.description: The physician explains the diagnosis, the nurse removes lines, gives written instructions and prescriptions and books or recommends follow-up at a clinic or with the family physician. The visit summary is faxed or sent electronically to the family physician and the chart goes to coding.

evidence.note: Volume from hosp-ed-discharge-home (2026-11-24): ED visits of 10,530 to 13,420 a month (organisation file) times the discharged-home share of NACRS visits, 78.8% to 79.9% in 2018/19 to 2021/22 (cihi_nacrs). The organisation file's 8,800 to 11,400 (mode 10,900, about 84%) leaves too little room for admissions (11%), patients who leave without being seen (4.5% to 6.9%) and transfers (about 2.5%).

process_map.name: Transfer patients to and from other hospitals
process_map.description: For services not offered locally, such as cardiac catheterization, neurosurgery or high-risk neonatal care, the physician calls CritiCall Ontario, which finds an accepting hospital; the team prepares records and images and books paramedic or air transport. Finding a bed can take hours.

surge.cause: COVID-19 waves (2020-2022)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from Ontario's 2020-2022 waves, when ICU demand exceeded base capacity and patients were moved between hospitals (478 incident management transfers to June 2021, src2).
Author's estimate for a community hospital without tertiary services.

process_map.name: Provide daily inpatient medical and nursing care
process_map.description: Hospitalists and specialists round daily, review results and write orders, and registered and practical nurses assess patients each shift, give care and document it. Most medical patients are frail older adults with several conditions, so plans change daily and length of stay grows when discharge is delayed.
process_map.unit_of_work: one inpatient stay on a medicine unit

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: occupancy runs above 100% in winter with unfunded surge beds in hallways and lounges.
Author's estimate: medicine accounts for about half of inpatient discharges in a community hospital.

process_map.name: Administer medications on inpatient units
process_map.description: Nurses take doses from the automated dispensing cabinet or patient drawer, scan or check the patient and drug against the electronic medication administration record, give the dose and document it. Interruptions, look-alike drugs and late doses are the common errors.
process_map.unit_of_work: one inpatient day of medication passes

evidence.note: One case per occupied bed day (author's estimate of 639 beds at 90-100% occupancy, src4).

process_map.name: Respond to deteriorating inpatients
process_map.description: When a patient meets calling criteria or a nurse is worried, the critical care response team of an ICU nurse, respiratory therapist and sometimes an intensivist assesses at the bedside, stabilizes and decides on ICU transfer. Late recognition of deterioration is the main risk.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of about 5 calls per 100 admissions.

process_map.name: Provide intensive care
process_map.description: Intensivists and critical care nurses at one nurse to one or two patients manage ventilated and unstable patients, with respiratory therapists running ventilators. ICU beds are few and full, so new admissions depend on stepping patients down to wards that are themselves full.

surge.cause: COVID-19 waves (2020-2022)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from Ontario's 2020-2022 waves, when ICU demand exceeded base capacity and patients were moved between hospitals (478 incident management transfers to June 2021, src2).
Author's estimate for about 30 ICU beds with an average stay of about 5-6 days.

process_map.name: Provide in-centre hemodialysis
process_map.description: Patients with kidney failure come three times a week for four-hour sessions; dialysis nurses cannulate, run and monitor the machines under nephrologist orders, and draw monthly blood work. Chair schedules are fixed, so a missed or late session pushes the whole shift.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Provide complex continuing care, rehabilitation and transitional care
process_map.description: Patients who no longer need acute care but cannot yet go home or are waiting for long-term care move to complex continuing care, rehabilitation or the regional transitional unit, where nurses and therapists work on function and the team works on discharge. Stays are long and admissions depend on beds freeing up.
process_map.unit_of_work: one admission to complex, rehabilitation or transitional care

evidence.note: Bed types from src4; admission volume is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Provide end-of-life care and manage deaths
process_map.description: The team holds goals-of-care conversations, provides palliative symptom care, and after a death a physician or nurse pronounces, completes the death certificate, notifies the coroner when required and makes the routine call to the donation agency. Missed donation notifications are a reported quality gap.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 3-4% of inpatient stays end in death.

process_map.name: Book elective surgery and manage the wait list
process_map.description: The surgeon's office faxes a booking package; the booking coordinator checks it is complete, enters the case and its priority in the hospital and provincial wait time systems and offers a date within the surgeon's block. Incomplete packages and patient cancellations cause rework.

surge.cause: Fiscal year-end push to complete funded procedure volumes (February-March)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; hospitals fund volumes per quality-based procedure (src10) and add cases before March 31.

Author's estimate: elective cases are about 80% of the reported surgeries (src1-src3). Revised 2026-11-24: elective bookings are about 87% of operating room cases (the Auditor General gives 13% emergencies), about 2,150 a month, now that endoscopies are counted only in sx-endoscopy.

process_map.name: Assess patients before surgery
process_map.description: Patients for inpatient or complex day surgery see a pre-admission nurse, have blood work and ECG as needed and are reviewed by an anesthesiologist, who may defer surgery until a condition is optimized. Missing results found on the day of surgery cancel cases.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about a quarter of elective surgical patients attend a pre-admission clinic.

process_map.name: Build the operating room schedule
process_map.description: Each week the scheduler fills surgeons' allocated blocks with booked cases, checks equipment, implant and bed needs and publishes the next day's slate; daily huddles adjust for add-on cases and cancellations. Over-running lists and late starts are the main source of lost OR time.

evidence.note: Weekly cycle with daily revisions; author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Perform a surgical case from admission to recovery
process_map.description: On the day of surgery the patient is admitted to same-day surgery, the OR team does the surgical safety checklist, the anesthesiologist and surgeon perform the case with OR nurses, and the patient recovers in the post-anaesthesia unit before going home or to a ward. Turnover time between cases and PACU holds set the day's throughput. Cases are operating room surgeries; endoscopies, which the annual reports include in surgeries, run through sx-endoscopy.

surge.cause: Fiscal year-end push to complete funded procedure volumes (February-March)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; quality-based procedure funding (src10) rewards completing volumes before March 31.

Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals. Revised 2026-11-24: operating room cases are the reported surgeries less endoscopies (about 1,300 a month, counted in sx-endoscopy and done in the endoscopy rooms), about 2,450 a month. Previously all 3,700 reported surgeries went through the operating rooms, which needed about twice the room hours the 17 rooms have.

process_map.name: Book and perform urgent and emergency surgery
process_map.description: Urgent cases from the ED or wards are booked on the add-on list by priority class; they go into the emergency room or bump elective cases, and night cases need the on-call team. Waits for an OR are a known cause of longer stays for hip fractures and appendicitis.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 12% of cases are urgent or emergent. Revised 2026-11-24: add-on cases are about 13% of operating room cases (Auditor General of Ontario), about 320 a month.

process_map.name: Provide post-operative inpatient care
process_map.description: Surgical patients recover on surgical units where nurses manage pain, wounds, drains and mobility and surgeons round early before the OR. Discharge follows care pathways for common procedures such as joint replacement, and delays come from home supports and late rounds.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from 115 surgical beds (src4 split) at about a 6-day average stay.

process_map.name: Reprocess surgical instruments and scopes
process_map.description: Used instruments come back from the OR, are washed, inspected, assembled into trays against count sheets, sterilized and stored, with priority for the next day's cases and flash requests. Missing or wet trays delay cases and incomplete trays are a frequent incident.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of about 2.5 trays per surgical or endoscopy case.

process_map.name: Perform endoscopy procedures
process_map.description: Patients referred for colonoscopy or gastroscopy are booked, prepared and sedated, the endoscopist does the procedure with an endoscopy nurse, biopsies go to pathology and scopes go for reprocessing. Poor bowel preparation and scope availability limit throughput.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; endoscopy volumes may be partly counted in the reported surgeries. Revised 2026-11-24: the reported surgeries include these procedures, so they are no longer also counted as operating room cases.

process_map.name: Run the fracture clinic
process_map.description: Patients sent from the ED with fractures are seen by orthopaedic surgeons with orthopaedic technologists who apply and remove casts; repeat X-rays are ordered and some patients are booked for surgery. Clinics are overbooked and depend on same-day imaging.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Ramp surgery down and back up under provincial directives
process_map.description: In 2020-2022 provincial directives paused non-urgent surgery during COVID-19 waves; the program re-prioritized the wait list, reallocated OR time and staff, and wrote recovery plans for extra funded volumes. Each restart depended on bed and staffing capacity.

evidence.note: Surgeries fell from 44,044 (2018/19) to 38,739 (2020/21) and recovered to 45,256 (2021/22); the planning work described is the author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Assess pregnant patients in obstetrical triage
process_map.description: Pregnant patients over about 20 weeks go straight to obstetrical triage, where a labour nurse assesses mother and fetus and a physician or midwife decides on admission in labour, observation or discharge. Volume is unpredictable and peaks at night.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of about two triage visits per birth.

process_map.name: Support labour and birth
process_map.description: Labour and delivery nurses care one to one in active labour, with an obstetrician, family physician or midwife attending the birth; about one in three births is a caesarean section in the obstetrical OR. The unit runs at the pace of unscheduled labour and must keep a room and team free for emergencies.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals. Giving birth is the most common reason for hospital stays in Canada and caesarean section the most common surgery (src9).

process_map.name: Provide postpartum and newborn care
process_map.description: Mother and baby stay together for one to two days while nurses support feeding and recovery, newborn screening and hearing tests are done, and the birth is recorded for the provincial registry. Discharge timing depends on feeding, jaundice checks and the physician's rounds.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals. Average stay for birth is about 2 days (src9).

process_map.name: Provide level II neonatal care
process_map.description: Premature or unwell newborns are admitted to the special care nursery for breathing support, feeding and jaundice treatment under paediatricians; babies who need level III care are transferred to a regional centre. Bassinets fill quickly and transfers wait for distant beds.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 10-12% of newborns need special care nursery admission.

process_map.name: Provide paediatric inpatient care
process_map.description: Children admitted from the ED with conditions such as bronchiolitis, asthma or dehydration are cared for by paediatricians and paediatric nurses, with family at the bedside. Admissions swing with respiratory virus season.

surge.cause: Paediatric respiratory virus season (RSV and influenza)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; paediatric admissions rise more than adult admissions in winter.
Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Assess mental health crises in the emergency department
process_map.description: After medical clearance, a crisis clinician assesses risk and needs, and the psychiatrist decides on admission, involuntary assessment under the Mental Health Act or discharge with community follow-up. Patients held on Mental Health Act forms often wait many hours in the ED for a bed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 3-4% of ED visits get a crisis assessment.

process_map.name: Provide inpatient psychiatric care
process_map.description: Voluntary and involuntary patients are admitted to the psychiatric unit, where psychiatrists review status and treatment, nurses provide observation and therapy, and rights advice and Consent and Capacity Board hearings follow when patients challenge their status. Discharge depends on housing and community supports.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from 40 beds at an average stay of about 11 days.

process_map.name: Run outpatient mental health and addictions clinics
process_map.description: Referrals from family physicians, the ED and inpatient units are screened by intake, wait-listed and booked with clinicians for assessment and therapy, with psychiatrist consultation as needed. Wait lists are long and no-shows are common.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Prepare for Consent and Capacity Board hearings
process_map.description: When a patient applies to review involuntary status or a finding of incapacity, the psychiatrist prepares a summary and evidence, health records are disclosed to counsel, and the hearing is held on the unit or by video within days. Hearings take psychiatrists away from clinical work.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Collect and receive laboratory specimens
process_map.description: Laboratory assistants draw blood on early-morning ward rounds, in the outpatient collection centre and in the ED, label tubes at the bedside and send them by pneumatic tube or porter; specimens are received, checked and accessioned. Mislabelled and haemolysed samples must be redrawn.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; testing volume rose with COVID-19 testing in 2020-2022.
Author's estimate: about eight tests per collection, applied to the lab tests driver (src1-src3).

process_map.name: Run and verify laboratory tests
process_map.description: Specimens are loaded on automated chemistry and hematology lines; technologists review flags, rerun or dilute samples, phone critical values and verify results, which go to the patient record and the provincial lab information system. Turnaround for ED and stat tests is the key measure.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Send out referral tests
process_map.description: Tests the hospital does not perform, including specialized microbiology and at times COVID-19 PCR, are packaged and shipped to Public Health Ontario or reference laboratories, and results are tracked and filed when they return. Lost or delayed results need chasing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; much higher during COVID-19 testing peaks.

process_map.name: Provide blood for transfusion
process_map.description: The transfusion lab performs group and screen and crossmatch, issues blood components against orders and keeps inventory with Canadian Blood Services; nurses check and administer the unit at the bedside. Wrong-blood-in-tube errors are rare but serious.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a community hospital of this size.

process_map.name: Examine surgical and biopsy tissue
process_map.description: Tissue from the OR and endoscopy is accessioned, processed into slides and read by pathologists, who sign out reports to the surgeon and family physician. Cancer reports follow provincial synoptic reporting standards.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Book outpatient imaging
process_map.description: Faxed requisitions from family physicians and clinics are reviewed for appropriateness, protocolled by a radiologist for CT and MRI, prioritized and booked; patients get preparation instructions and MRI and CT waits are reported to the province. Incomplete requisitions and long MRI waits generate calls.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about a quarter of exams are booked outpatient exams.

process_map.name: Perform diagnostic imaging exams
process_map.description: Technologists and sonographers check the order, position and scan the patient, adjust protocols, and send images to PACS; emergency and inpatient exams are fitted around booked outpatients. CT demand from the ED and porter availability for inpatients drive the queues.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Read and report imaging exams
process_map.description: Radiologists read studies from a worklist by priority, dictate with voice recognition and sign reports; urgent findings are phoned to the ordering physician and ED studies after hours are read on call or by remote reading. Report turnaround for outpatients can stretch to days.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Assign inpatient beds and run patient flow
process_map.description: Patient flow coordinators match bed requests from the ED, OR, ICU and other hospitals to available and soon-to-be-clean beds, run twice-daily bed meetings with unit managers and open surge beds when the hospital is over capacity. Assignments wait on discharges, cleaning and isolation needs.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: occupancy runs above 100% in winter with unfunded surge beds in hallways and lounges.
Author's estimate: admissions plus internal transfers.

process_map.name: Verify and dispense medication orders
process_map.description: Pharmacists review each new order for dose, interactions and allergies, technicians fill unit doses, IV admixtures and cabinet refills, and pharmacists check the product before release. Order queues back up after morning rounds and admission surges.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of about three new orders per patient day plus ED and clinic orders.

process_map.name: Buy and control pharmacy drug inventory
process_map.description: Technicians reorder drugs from the wholesaler against par levels, receive deliveries, manage shortages and recalls, and count and reconcile controlled substances in cabinets and the pharmacy vault. Drug shortages force substitutions and extra work.

evidence.note: Daily ordering cycle; author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Assess and treat inpatients referred to allied health
process_map.description: Physiotherapists, occupational therapists, social workers, dietitians and speech-language pathologists pick up referrals from the electronic record, prioritize discharge-critical patients, assess and treat, and document recommendations. Weekend coverage is thin, so Friday referrals wait.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of about two to three referrals per inpatient stay.

process_map.name: Plan discharges and transitions from inpatient units
process_map.description: From admission the team sets an expected discharge date; social workers and home care coordinators arrange home services or placement, the physician writes the discharge order and summary, and nurses teach the patient and family. Late-day discharges and waits for home care slow bed turnover.
process_map.unit_of_work: one inpatient discharge from a medicine, surgical or complex care unit

evidence.note: Volume from hosp-cs-discharge-planning (2026-11-24): Organisation file gives 2,000 to 2,600 inpatient discharges a month for all units. The author removes about 360 obstetric, 100 paediatric and 120 psychiatric discharges a month (births driver 333 to 391 a month and unit sizes in the organisation file).

process_map.name: Manage patients waiting for an alternate level of care
process_map.description: When a physician designates a patient as alternate level of care, the team applies for long-term care, rehabilitation or other settings, tracks offers and moves patients to transitional beds; ALC days are reported to the province. ALC patients can occupy a large share of acute beds, which blocks admissions from the ED.

evidence.note: ALC defined by CIHI; 5.8% of stays nationally include ALC days (src9); the 35-bed regional ALC unit is listed in src4. Volume is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Receive referrals and book outpatient clinics
process_map.description: Clinic clerks receive faxed referrals, check completeness, have the specialist triage urgency, add the patient to the wait list and book appointments and reminders. Faxes get lost or duplicated, and incomplete referrals bounce back to the referring office.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 30% of clinic visits are new referrals.

process_map.name: Hold outpatient specialty clinic visits
process_map.description: Patients are registered, roomed by a clinic nurse and seen by the specialist, who orders tests, books follow-up or surgery and dictates a letter to the referring physician. Clinics run late when physicians come from the OR or wards.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Give chemotherapy and systemic therapy
process_map.description: Oncologists from the regional cancer program order regimens, pharmacy prepares doses, and chemotherapy nurses check blood work, give treatment in chairs and monitor for reactions; activity is reported to the regional cancer program. Late blood results and pharmacy preparation time delay chair starts.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Run COVID-19 assessment centres
process_map.description: From 2020 to 2022 the corporation ran three testing centres where people were screened, registered, swabbed and sent results, with specimens going to hospital and public health laboratories. Demand swung with each wave and with changing provincial eligibility rules.

surge.cause: COVID-19 waves and testing eligibility changes (2020-2022)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of testing demand peaks.
Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Run the COVID-19 vaccination clinic
process_map.description: From 2021 the hospital ran a mass vaccination clinic: people booked online, were screened, vaccinated by nurses and observed for 15 minutes, and each dose was recorded in the provincial system. Supply and eligibility changed week to week.

surge.cause: Vaccine eligibility expansions and booster campaigns (2021-2022)

evidence.note: Author's estimate.
Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Report and review patient safety incidents
process_map.description: Staff report incidents in the safety reporting system; managers review and follow up, risk specialists triage serious events, and critical incidents get a formal review, disclosure to the patient and reports to the Medical Advisory Committee and board quality committee. Under-reporting and slow manager follow-up are common.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of about 3 reports per 100 patient days.

process_map.name: Handle patient complaints and compliments
process_map.description: The patient relations specialist logs complaints, contacts the patient, involves the unit manager or physician leader, and responds within the policy timeline; unresolved complaints may go to the Patient Ombudsman. Complaints about waits and communication dominate.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Prevent and control infections
process_map.description: Infection control practitioners review positive lab results and admissions, place and lift isolation, run surveillance for hospital-acquired infections, report diseases of public health significance and manage outbreaks with the public health unit. In 2020-2022 COVID-19 screening, testing and outbreak work multiplied the load.
process_map.unit_of_work: one isolation case or outbreak action

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: isolation cases and outbreaks multiply in respiratory season and COVID-19 waves.
Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Prepare the annual quality improvement plan
process_map.description: Each year the quality team selects indicators and targets using provincial priorities, consults patients and staff, gets board approval and submits and posts the plan by April 1; progress is reported to the board quality committee quarterly. Data lags make targets hard to track.

evidence.note: QIP timing and public posting from src6.

process_map.name: Prepare for and complete accreditation
process_map.description: On a multi-year cycle the hospital completes self-assessments and staff surveys against national standards and required practices, fixes gaps, hosts surveyors and acts on follow-ups. Preparation pulls managers and educators away from operations for months.

evidence.note: Accreditation against standards (src11); the corporation holds Exemplary Standing (src4). Cycle length of about four years in the period is the author's knowledge.

process_map.name: Manage privacy breaches
process_map.description: Audits of record access and staff reports reveal snooping, misdirected faxes and lost documents; the privacy officer contains the breach, notifies affected patients and reports to the privacy commissioner when required. Misdirected faxes are the most common cause.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Plan the annual operating and capital budget
process_map.description: Finance builds the budget from the provincial funding letter, funded procedure volumes, wage settlements and program requests, sets capital priorities with foundation funding, and takes it to the board; the planning submission goes to the province and Ontario Health. Funding letters often arrive after the fiscal year starts.

evidence.note: Ministry revenue grew from $374.9M (2018/19) to $513.5M (2021/22) of total revenue $475M to $592M (src1, src3); global budget plus quality-based procedure funding (src10).

process_map.name: Report performance under the accountability agreement
process_map.description: Each quarter finance and decision support compile the trial balance, service volumes and indicators against the hospital service accountability agreement and submit them, explaining variances. Coding completeness and late data affect the volumes reported.

evidence.note: Quarterly cycle; author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Close the books each month
process_map.description: Accountants post payroll, accounts payable, revenue and accruals, reconcile accounts, run variance reports for cost centre managers and produce monthly results for the executive and board. Payroll and supply accruals are the main sources of late adjustments.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Complete the year-end audit
process_map.description: After March 31 finance prepares year-end schedules, supports the external auditor's testing and drafts the financial statements, which the audit committee and board approve and the hospital publishes. Deferred grant and capital accounting take the most effort.

evidence.note: The corporation publishes audited financial statements (src5) and a financial summary in its annual report (src1).

process_map.name: Pay supplier invoices
process_map.description: AP clerks match supplier invoices to purchase orders and goods receipts in the ERP, resolve price and quantity mismatches with buyers and departments, and release payments in weekly runs. Non-PO invoices need manual approval routing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Run competitive procurements
process_map.description: Buyers run competitive procurements following broader public sector rules for goods and services above set thresholds, often through a shared group purchasing organization, evaluate bids with clinical users and award contracts. Clinical product trials and evaluation committees stretch timelines.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Replenish supplies to clinical units
process_map.description: Stores clerks count par levels on units, pick and deliver supplies, build OR case carts, place purchase orders and receive deliveries at the dock. Stock-outs on units lead to borrowing and urgent orders, and PPE was rationed in 2020.

surge.cause: COVID-19 personal protective equipment demand (2020-2021)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; PPE use and shortages peaked in 2020.
Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Bill uninsured patients and third parties
process_map.description: Patient accounts clerks bill uninsured and out-of-country patients, preferred accommodation, other provinces and WSIB, and chase unpaid accounts. Uninsured ED visits are hard to collect.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Recruit and onboard staff
process_map.description: Managers raise requisitions, recruiters post jobs under collective agreement seniority rules, screen and interview candidates, run reference and police checks, and new hires get occupational health clearance and corporate and clinical orientation. Nursing vacancies grew through 2021-2022.

surge.cause: Spring and summer hiring of new graduate nurses

evidence.note: Author's estimate.
Author's estimate from staff growing from 4,022 to 5,228 in three years (src1, src3) plus about 10% turnover.

process_map.name: Schedule shifts and fill sick calls
process_map.description: Schedules are built for six-week periods under collective agreement rules; each day the staffing office takes sick calls and requests for extra staff, offers shifts by seniority and part-time availability and escalates to overtime or agency staff when needed. Unfilled shifts lead to closed beds or short-staffed units.

surge.cause: Staff illness and isolation in respiratory season and COVID-19 waves

evidence.note: Author's estimate: sick calls and exclusions rise sharply in winter and during COVID-19 waves.
Author's estimate from about 3,000 nursing and support staff with 4-6% daily absence.

process_map.name: Run biweekly payroll
process_map.description: Payroll administrators import worked hours, premiums and absences from time and attendance, apply collective agreement rules and retroactive wage settlements, run the pay, remit deductions and post costs to the ledger. Premium and retro pay errors cause many queries.

evidence.note: 26 pay runs a year; author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Manage grievances and labour relations
process_map.description: HR advisors meet union representatives on grievances about scheduling, discipline and premiums, negotiate settlements and prepare arbitration cases; central bargaining sets wages for hospital nurses and others. Wage restraint under Bill 124 (2019-2022) shaped relations.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Manage occupational health and workplace safety
process_map.description: Occupational health nurses clear new hires' immunizations, run fit testing and flu campaigns, follow up staff exposures and injuries, file WSIB reports and manage return to work. COVID-19 staff screening, testing and isolation clearance added large volumes in 2020-2022.

surge.cause: Staff illness and isolation in respiratory season and COVID-19 waves

evidence.note: Author's estimate: sick calls and exclusions rise sharply in winter and during COVID-19 waves.
Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Register outpatient, inpatient and diagnostic visits
process_map.description: Registration clerks verify identity and health card eligibility, create or update the patient record and visit, and flag uninsured patients for billing. Duplicate records and wrong patient selection are the main data quality problems.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: registered visits other than ED registrations.

process_map.name: Code and abstract charts for CIHI
process_map.description: After discharge, coders review the completed chart, assign diagnosis and intervention codes and abstract each inpatient stay, day surgery and ED visit for CIHI, querying physicians when documentation is unclear. Coded data drives provincial funding, so incomplete charts at month end are chased.

evidence.note: ED visits must be reported to NACRS in Ontario (src8); coded data feeds procedure-based funding (src10). Volume is the author's estimate.

process_map.name: Release health records
process_map.description: Health records clerks log requests from patients, lawyers and insurers, confirm consent or legal authority, pull and review records and release copies within the statutory timeline. Requests involving mental health or third-party information need closer review.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Transcribe dictations and complete charts
process_map.description: Transcriptionists type or edit voice-recognized dictations of discharge summaries, consults and operative notes, which physicians then sign; paper forms are scanned into the record. Unsigned dictations hold up chart completion and coding.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Resolve IT incidents and requests
process_map.description: The service desk logs calls and tickets, resets passwords, sets up access for new staff and physicians, and routes clinical system and device problems to analysts or vendors. Downtime of clinical systems triggers paper downtime procedures.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Change and upgrade clinical systems
process_map.description: Analysts gather requests, configure order sets, forms and interfaces, test with clinical users, get change approval and release changes, coordinating vendor upgrades and provincial reporting changes. Testing capacity limits how many changes go live.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Clean beds after discharge
process_map.description: When a discharge is entered, the bed board alerts environmental services; an aide strips and cleans the room, with extra steps for isolation rooms, and marks the bed clean. Evening discharges meet a smaller night crew, so beds sit dirty while the ED waits.

surge.cause: Winter respiratory virus season (influenza and RSV; COVID-19 waves from 2020)

evidence.note: Author's estimate: occupancy runs above 100% in winter with unfunded surge beds in hallways and lounges.
Author's estimate: discharges plus transfers and isolation cleans.

process_map.name: Move patients within the hospitals
process_map.description: Porters take dispatch requests to move patients between units, imaging, the OR and discharge areas, by wheelchair or stretcher. Delays at peak hours hold up imaging and OR starts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Prepare and deliver patient meals
process_map.description: The diet office takes diet orders and menu choices, cooks and food service workers assemble trays in the kitchen and deliver them to units three times a day. Late diet changes and missed trays after transfers are common.

evidence.note: Volume from the corporation's annual reports; description of the work is the author's general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

process_map.name: Maintain buildings and handle work orders
process_map.description: Maintenance staff take work orders for repairs, run preventive maintenance on building systems and keep 24-hour cover for utilities, medical gases and elevators, contracting specialized work. Infection control precautions add steps for work in patient areas.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Service medical equipment
process_map.description: Biomedical technologists inspect, repair and do preventive maintenance on pumps, monitors and other devices, manage vendor service for imaging equipment and report serious device incidents. Equipment out for repair is a frequent complaint on units.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Respond to security calls and violent incidents
process_map.description: Security officers patrol, respond to calls and code whites, stand by with patients held under the Mental Health Act and report incidents. Violence against staff in the ED and mental health units is a reported workplace safety problem.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

process_map.name: Plan for emergencies and surges
process_map.description: The emergency preparedness coordinator maintains emergency codes and surge plans, runs drills and leads the hospital's incident management structure when a code orange, outage or pandemic surge is declared. The COVID-19 incident command ran for most of 2020-2022.

surge.cause: Major incident or pandemic surge activation

evidence.note: Author's estimate.
478 incident management system transfers recorded to June 2021 (src2); the planning work described is the author's general knowledge.

process_map.name: Appoint and reappoint medical staff
process_map.description: Applicants and existing physicians, midwives and dentists submit applications; the medical affairs office verifies licences, insurance and references, the department chief recommends, the credentials committee and Medical Advisory Committee review and the board grants privileges. The annual reappointment cycle creates a heavy peak.

surge.cause: Annual reappointment cycle

evidence.note: Author's estimate.
Author's estimate from about 800-930 credentialed staff (src1-src3) reappointed yearly.

process_map.name: Run the Medical Advisory Committee
process_map.description: The chief of staff chairs the monthly Medical Advisory Committee of department chiefs, which reviews credentialing, critical incident and quality reports, medical staff rules and on-call issues, and makes recommendations to the board. Agendas are long and follow-ups slow.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of Ontario hospital governance.

process_map.name: Run the board and committee cycle
process_map.description: The board secretariat assembles packages for the board and its quality, finance and audit, and governance committees, executives present reports, and the board approves budgets, plans, privileges and the accountability agreement. Material prepared for the board takes executive time each month.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of Ontario public hospital governance.

process_map.name: Set strategy and plan capacity
process_map.description: Executives refresh the multi-year strategic plan with the board, staff and community, plan capacity such as beds and redevelopment, and set annual corporate priorities that feed the budget. Planning was largely displaced by pandemic response in 2020-2021.

evidence.note: The corporation publishes strategic plans (src5); the process is the author's general knowledge.

assumptions: The organisation is modelled on Halton Healthcare's public figures for fiscal years 2018/19 to 2021/22, generalised to a typical large multi-site Ontario community hospital; it is not a description of that hospital's internal processes.

profile.employees counts about 4,900 employed staff (the average of the reported 4,022, 5,089 and 5,228) plus 885 in the medical staff unit (873 credentialed physicians, midwives and dentists and 12 medical affairs employees). Credentialed staff are included because they do much of the clinical work in the processes, though most are paid by OHIP rather than the hospital.

Unit and role headcounts below the corporation total are the author's allocation using typical Ontario community hospital staffing; role headcounts are people, not FTEs, and many nursing staff are part-time.

Loaded cost per hour for employees is the estimated 2019-2022 hourly wage multiplied by 1.35 (benefits and HOOPP pension about 25%, overhead about 10%). Physician costs are gross clinical earnings estimates paid by the province.

Bed counts come from a 2024 directory listing (src4) split across services by the author; other physical capacity (ED spaces, ORs, scanners, dialysis stations, chairs) is estimated from reported volumes.
Annual volumes are divided by 12 for cases_per_month; low and high reflect the range across 2018/19 to 2021/22, including the 2020/21 pandemic dip in ED visits and surgeries.

The 2020-2022 COVID-19 processes (assessment centres, vaccination clinic, field hospital beds, surgical ramp-down) are included because they fall in the reference period; they did not run before March 2020.

Legislation named in descriptions (Public Hospitals Act, Mental Health Act, Excellent Care for All Act, PHIPA, Occupational Health and Safety Act, Bill 124) is from the author's general knowledge; the provincial e-Laws pages could not be opened, so no step relies on a section number.
CTAS triage levels and target times are from the author's general knowledge; the guideline documents found could not be opened.

Revised 2026-11-24: role headcounts were raised where the workflows record more work than the role could do, and roles first fill their units' unassigned headcount, so the employee total moves only where a unit's listed roles exceed it. Operating room cases exclude endoscopies, which the annual reports count as surgeries and the map counts in sx-endoscopy.
